VC3D line annotation: break tag on control points, gap spans between two breaks (#1879)

* VC3D line annotation: break tag on control points, gap spans between two breaks

A control point can be tagged `break` from its Ctrl+right-click menu, on
any point (the kollesis termination stays end-only). The tag is one more
string in the per-control-point `tags` array, so every loader since the
kollesis tag accepts it unchanged and untagged fibers are written exactly
as before. A point carries either tag, never both: adding the second is
disabled in the menu and refused by the handlers, removing either is
always possible, and a click that would collapse a break point with a
termination is refused rather than dropping a tag.

Two consecutive break points make the span between them a gap span, a
stretch where the papyrus is missing:

- drawn as a dotted amber line in place of the cyan line in the side cut,
  the strips and the overview bar, and as a dotted amber run bounded
  exactly at the two controls in the Fiber Map, on every fiber; the break
  points draw a dotted amber ring (rim in the map) one step larger than a
  filled point, keeping a link-state fill inside when linked;
- closed to placement: clicks, `/`, `0` and the current-position marker
  treat any line position strictly inside it as blocked until a break is
  removed;
- given the cubic-spline goal when it forms, and back to global when it
  dissolves while still a spline, through the same path as the menu's
  "Interpolation goal", so the line bridges the break instead of tracing
  for fiber signal across it. The tag itself is saved first, on its own,
  through the persist helper the kollesis toggle now shares.

Gap ranges are computed from the full control list in the overlay
builders, not from the plane-filtered markers, so a hidden endpoint or a
hidden untagged control between two visible breaks cannot read as a gap.
The Fiber Map carries the flags on the placed fiber (a lone break has no
run to express it) and hashes them in both session digests but not in the
geometry cache key, like the kollesis flags. Display-only in the map: heat
map seeding and winding evidence are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UfUjZiGYWsFpoiudi8pEtQ

* VC3D fibers: format version 4 with span tags; a gap is recorded on the span

Two consecutive break points still make the span between them a gap, but
the gap is now written on the span itself: version 4 adds an optional
`tags` array of strings to each `segment_to_next` descriptor, and VC3D puts
`gap` there exactly when both endpoint controls carry `break`. Everything
that shows or enforces a gap reads the span tag, never the pair of rings:
the dotted amber line in the side cut, strips and overview bar, the
placement block, the cubic-spline goal change, and the Fiber Map runs. Only
the dotted rings read the point tags. So a reader of the file learns the gap
from the span alone, and when the amber line looks right the span metadata
is right.

VC3D keeps the span tags in step with the break tags after the toggle, after
every structural edit (click collapse, delete, solve landing, superseded-
solve merge) and in every file it writes; a loaded file whose span tags
disagree with its break tags (a version-3 file, a hand edit) is healed on
load and saved back as version 4 under the adjacent-link heal's stale-file
guard. The span label appends "gap" to the mode marker. Span tags survive a
re-solve like the goal does, and the lasagna line probe carries them through
a re-optimization.

Version 4 is version 3 plus the span tags, written only when non-empty; a
version-3 span carrying tags is rejected so the version is a true signal.
The core strict loader, VC3D, the python format package and fiber_merge
accept 1, 3 and 4. fiber_merge treats 3 and 4 as one lineage (a v3 base with
v4 sides is the normal state after an upgrade, not a version conflict) and
writes the merge as version 4 when any side is 4. Builds older than this
refuse version-4 files.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UfUjZiGYWsFpoiudi8pEtQ

* VC3D line annotation: span menu on the strips (goal, gap, damaged, split); split candidate removed

In the strip views a Ctrl+right-click on the centre line away from every
control point marker opens a menu for the span containing the click, so a
span action is never ambiguous about its span: within a marker's reach the
point menu opens as before, far from both the nearest-point fallback stands.
The span menu shows the span's state (mode, goal, gap or damaged) and holds
everything that acts on a span:

- Interpolation goal, moved here from the point menu (it was applied to the
  span under the cut position, not the click).
- Gap: tags both ends as breaks, which makes the span a gap through the
  usual sync and goal policy. A break is now refused at or immediately next
  to a kollesis termination, from both menus, so the span at a sheet join can
  never become a gap. Unchecking removes the break only from ends no other
  gap span depends on.
- Damaged: a new span tag, `damaged`, for a correctly followed span whose
  papyrus is damaged. Changes nothing about the points, the goal or the
  geometry; never on a gap span (the gap wins and clears it). Drawn as
  alternating amber and red dashes, two dashed strokes half a period apart
  (OverlayStyle gained a dashOffset for this), in the side cut, strips,
  overview bar and Fiber Map; the span label appends "damaged".
- Split, different windings / Split and link, same winding: remove the span.
  Both halves are saved as new fibers with the reoptimization tag and their
  links remapped, the original is deleted and its workspace closes; nothing
  is reopened. The link variant records a pending link between the new ends.

The split-candidate tooling is gone: the red candidate marker, "Designate as
split candidate", "Split from candidate" and "... and link", their signals,
menu states and handlers. The split body is reused by the span split.

The tag-persist helper became a generic per-control edit-and-persist core
(guards, edit, gap sync, save with undo, mirroring to peer panes by nearest
position, overlay refresh) that the point-tag toggles and the damaged toggle
share; the break toggle and the span gap share the goal reconciliation.
